death.note: Placed by the passing his own page dates him against. saint.gr’s whole account of the pair is that they "were martyred by the sword at Caesarea, of Cappadocia, at the time when the proconsul of Nicomedia Perinios was bringing the martyr Codratus there"; `codratus-of-nicomedia` carries 249–259, the two reigns his page names. The page "does not say whether they were of Codratus’s company or men whom his passing merely dated", and the interval is the same either way.

source.text: saint.gr, το εορτολόγιο της 7ης Μαΐου — «Άγιοι Ρουφίνος και Σατορνίνος»

attestations.note: The life page heads «Τύπος εορτής: Σταθερή. Εορτάζει στις 7 Μαΐου εκάστου έτους», the same day as the listing, and gives each of the two a head line. A pair the page enumerates is two folders. **The page dates them only by another man's journey**: they died at Caesarea of Cappadocia «την εποχή που ο ανθύπατος Νικομηδείας Περίνιος, οδηγούσε εκεί τον μάρτυρα Κοδράτο» — while the proconsul was bringing Codratus there — and it prints no year of its own for them, so `dates` stays absent even though Codratus's own page names the reigns of Decius and Valerian. That inference is not made here. **He is none of the corpus's Saturnini or Rufinas**, who are all in other companies on other days. No manner of trial, no judge of their own, no relics, no hymn.
